paragraphs: Teacher Kim put a poster of school clubs on the wall. Football was on Monday, and violin was on Tuesday. "You may join only one club this year," said Teacher Kim. Mia looked at the poster for a long time. She had a football and a violin at home. "Which club do I like more?" she asked Lily. "I can guess," said Lily. "Let me watch you for two days."

On Monday, Mia tried the football club with Coach Matt. The sun was hot, and the children ran. Mia ran too. Coach Matt was kind, and he gave Mia a bottle of water. She kicked the ball badly, and it went far away. Lily watched from the grass. Mia did not smile. After ten minutes, she looked at the gate. "I want to go home," she said quietly.

On Tuesday, Mia carried her violin to the music room. The bag was very heavy, but she did not ask for help. She played badly, and the sound was high and funny. The music room was quiet and cool. Mia laughed, and then she played again. She smiled more than on Monday. Lily listened and smiled too.

After school, Lily said, "I guess you like the violin more than football." "You are right," said Mia. "But I play so badly." "You are better than last week," said Lily. "And you smile more with the violin." Mia smiled and gave Lily a big hug. Mia joined the violin club on Wednesday. At home, Snow sat next to the violin and listened. Mia joined the violin club, and Snow listened to every song.
